description: CarMax started as a solution for consumers who dreaded a trip to the car dealer. Emphasizing a stress-free experience, it introduced the concept of “no-haggle” purchasing through slogans like “You shouldn’t have to argue to get a fair price.” Now CarMax is the largest U.S. retailer for used cars with 250 stores nationwide and a portfolio of assets worth nearly $18 billion. In its fiscal year ended February 2025, the company sold roughly 790,000 pre-owned vehicles and another 540,000 wholesale vehicles at auctions.

title: CarMax

rankings.title: Best Large Workplaces in Retail
rankings.itemDescription:
Employees say:

"The amount of interdepartmental growth that can be achieved by networking and expressing interest to learn is one of the biggest unique things I've seen compared to other companies. Simply saying that you may want to learn another part of the store results in other associates or the management team taking you under their wing to give a little taste of what the other department is like. Coming from Inventory, I was taught how to detail, how to do interior repairs, how to do minor prep work, how to fill out titles, among other things just because I asked, as well as fostering growth through a culture of learning rather than consequences for trying to learn or attempt something."

rankings.title: Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For
rankings.itemDescription:
Employees say:

"I love working for CarMax and I will retire with CarMax. CarMax truly cares about the individual, whether customer, associate or community. CarMax is more than a place to work and make money, it completely changed my life. I feel like my personal values align with the CarMax core values and CarMax truly embraces each associate for their own authentic self. I have grown my career from an hourly associate to a Senior Manager and I have felt so much support. I have built financial success in my life through CarMax valuing me as an individual, having honest conversations on where I can improve as well as recognizing me for the strengths I bring to the table. CarMax is the best place to work!"

This is the 20th year that CarMax, a used autos retailer, has appeared on the list.

 

The company has started using AI to support business processes and consumer-facing content, such as car reviews, to help free up employees' time. In addition, CarMax is using AI to power multiple customer experiences, such as giving online offers to customers to sell their car to CarMax in minutes, and providing personalized car recommendations to help customers buy their next car from CarMax quickly. CarMax also invests in its virtual AI assistant, Skye, to help streamline its customer experience centers and support customers as they are shopping, through steps like vehicle shipping and appointment preparation and management.
 

For CarMax, community involvement is big. One of its longest-lasting key relationships is with KABOOM!, an accredited charity that builds playgrounds in underfunded and underinvested communities. Since the partnership formed in 2011, more than 11,000 employees have come together to build 206 play spaces.

rankings.title: Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For
rankings.itemDescription:
The no-haggle retailer of used autos is appearing on the Best Companies to Work For list for the 19th time this year.

  • New hires receive a warm welcome even before their first day. As soon as someone accepts a job offer, the team leader calls to welcome them, and a mentor calls to answer any questions they might have before they start.

  • Elaborate onboarding includes making sure new hires have clear direction about their schedule and are provided with smaller details, such as where they should park and what restaurants are nearby, before their first day.

  • Workers can utilize the CarMax Connect web platform to get personalized information, aggregated news, and useful company resources.

  • “It's the first company that I've worked for that makes you feel the company puts its employees first, and truly understands that it's the sum of its parts that make up the whole,” said one employee. “They're also very understanding when it comes to personal issues getting in the way of work and allowing you to take time off to address them, and not make you feel like you're letting the whole company down for doing so.”

rankings.title: Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For
rankings.itemDescription: CarMax, the nation’s leading used-car retailer, believes that good customer service begins with treating employees right. At the peak of the pandemic, every CarMax manager met with their associates to help them balance work and family life. As a result, some employees were able to modify their schedules or take a leave of absence that enabled them to continue receiving benefits. And CarMax aims to hold itself to a high standard; associates with concerns over safety or ethics are encouraged to speak up via an open door policy. “The most amazing thing about working here is our managers genuinely care about us,” says one employee. “They will put in extra time and effort to help us with anything we need, even if it’s something in our personal life.”

rankings.title: Best Large Workplaces in Retail
rankings.itemDescription:
Employees say:

“I feel that everyone here is welcoming and accepting of everyone. We are encouraged to develop relationships within our department as well as others. We are empowered to make decisions we feel are necessary in the moment whether it is business or customer related. I can be myself at work and that is a great feeling. I feel people have the best interests of everyone on a personal as well as professional level.”

rankings.title: Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For
rankings.itemDescription: When closures led to furloughs of some employees, it wasn’t just hourly workers who felt the squeeze. “I appreciated that executives took a pay cut and that the board of trustees did not receive any compensation,” one employee writes. (Indeed, CEO William Nash took a 50% cut.) The company covered health insurance premiums for furloughed workers, and an associate disaster relief fund enabled employees to apply for help if they became ill or experienced a qualifying hardship. By the end of July 2020, CarMax no longer had any associates on furlough, and positions had been made available for approximately 99% of impacted employees.
